The browser never fetches a separate blob file — an avatar is a base64 data URI stored in the `user.avatar_url` column, and the API rewrites it to a `/file/...` URL so responses stay small. **Hops** 1. `convertUserFromStore` (emits the URL `/file/users/{username}/avatar`) — server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go:36 2. `UserAvatar` (browser ``) — web/src/components/UserAvatar.tsx:14 3. `RegisterRoutes` — route `GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar` — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:121-125 (wired in server/server.go:81) 4. `serveUserAvatar` (the serving handler) — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:168 5. `getCurrentUser` → `authenticator.AuthenticateToUser` (only when `!Profile.AllowAnonymous()`; private instances reject anonymous viewers) — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:708 6. `getUserByUsername` — builds `store.FindUser{Username: &identifier}` — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:715 7. `Store.GetUser` — server/../store/user.go:148 (the `userCache` fast path is keyed by ID only, so a username lookup always falls through) 8. `Store.ListUsers` — store/user.go:136 9. `driver.ListUsers` (interface) — store/driver.go:47 10. `DB.ListUsers` — `SELECT … avatar_url … FROM user WHERE username = ?`, scanned into `User.AvatarURL` — store/db/sqlite/user.go:88 (Postgres equivalent: store/db/postgres/user.go:87) 11. `parseDataURI` — splits the stored `data:;base64,…` value into MIME type + bytes — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:737 12. `avatarAllowedTypes` gate, then `c.Blob` with `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` (`setSecurityHeaders`) and long `Cache-Control` — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:75, 201-209 One stale artifact worth noting: `"/memos.api.v1.UserService/GetUserAvatar"` is listed in the ACL allowlist at server/router/api/v1/acl_config.go:25, but no such gRPC method exists in the codebase — avatar serving is entirely the Echo route above.
